feedback: No race has been run for this geometry yet, and I have no earlier race evidence, so this feedback rests on the contract and on what the controller has to do with this sensor layout. The five sensors at 12 mm spacing with 12 mm footprints cover the 25 mm tape at all offsets within a few millimetres, so the controller does not need extra compensation for sensor gaps. The sensors sit 0.04 m ahead of the axle, which gives look-ahead but also means the signal reacts before the wheels reach the bend. If the next race shows line_loss_events above zero on the slalom or s-bend, the likely cause is that the sensor span is too narrow for the lateral swing of those bends, so widen the x span to roughly ±0.032 m. If the next race shows steering_oscillation high while line_loss_events stays at zero, the look-ahead is too long for the tight bends, so move the forward sensor row to y = 0.03 m. If the robot completes all three development tracks with low rms_error, keep the geometry and focus on reducing completion_time by lowering mass toward 0.5 kg.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is above zero on slalom or s-bend: widen sensor_positions to x = -0.032 to +0.032 m (keeping 5 sensors) to cover larger lateral swings, citing the expected line loss on tight bends from the contract's narrow 0.048 m span.
If steering_oscillation is high with no line loss: move the sensor row to y = 0.03 m to shorten look-ahead on tight bends, and test whether sensor_size 0.016 m reduces partial-reading noise.
If all development tracks complete with low rms_error: reduce mass to 0.5 kg to improve acceleration toward the 1.5 m/s average needed for completion_time under 3 s.
